just saw a pseud review of the Odyssey by the sort of person who doesn't realize Chris Nolan is an idiot. one of the things that stuck out to me is it points out Nolan's ongoing fixation with the passing of an age and being judged by the future, which is a wild inversion of, you know, The Odyssey

The Odyssey was very good and also pretty bloated in a way Nolan films tend to be.

They also cut out the part where the cyclops gives a delightful musical jig and I'll forever hate them for it.

The Odyssey is Nolan working at the peak of his powers when it comes to scale. Combines his love of depicting the very nature of storytelling, non linear structures and men faced with their regret of what they’ve wrought on the world. All spun into fantasy that he’s never stepped into.

In other news, I am still unpacking The Odyssey but it was a pretty astonishing piece of work. As someone who is middling on Oppenheimer and actively dislikes Tenet I am pleased to have a new Nolan movie I unequivocally enjoyed. I highly recommend you go and see it in the cinema.
